title: The Kannan-Tetali-Vempala switch-chain conjecture
formal: Do universal constants K,c>0 exist such that, for all r,s≥1 and all nonnegative integer margins a∈ℕ^r,b∈ℕ^s with a nonempty realization set Ω(a,b), the lazy switch chain below satisfies t_mix(1/4)≤K(r+s)^c?
context:
TCS-6254 and TCS-6412 concern degree-sequence realizability or modification, not mixing of the switch chain.

definitions: Ω(a,b) is the set of matrices M∈{0,1}^{r×s} with Σ_j M_ij=a_i and Σ_i M_ij=b_j. The state space is promised nonempty; no restriction on density or balance is imposed. At each discrete step, stay put with probability 1/2. Otherwise choose uniformly an unordered pair of distinct rows and independently an unordered pair of distinct columns. If their 2×2 submatrix is ((1,0),(0,1)) or ((0,1),(1,0)), replace it by the other pattern; otherwise stay put. If r<2 or s<2, the state space is a singleton and each step stays put. P denotes this transition matrix and π the uniform measure on Ω. Define t_mix(1/4)=min{t∈ℕ: max_{M∈Ω} (1/2)Σ_{N∈Ω}|P^t(M,N)−1/|Ω||≤1/4}, with value +∞ if the set is empty. Time counts attempted transitions, including stays. The maximum is over every initial state. The constants are independent of r,s and all margins; preprocessing, bit costs and sampling algorithms using other transitions are not part of this mixing-time question.
answer_criterion: Prove the proposition in the problem statement or prove its logical negation, using exactly the definitions, hypotheses and quantifier order stated here. The proof must cover the complete target.

sentences: A zero-one matrix with prescribed row and column sums can encode a bipartite graph with prescribed degrees.
The switch chain moves between such matrices by exchanging an alternating pattern in a two-by-two submatrix, preserving every required sum.
The conjecture asks whether a lazy version converges in polynomial time to its uniform stationary distribution for every nonempty set of feasible matrices.
An affirmative answer would justify a widely applicable local method for sampling constrained binary data.
The difficulty is controlling global bottlenecks across all feasible margins, rather than merely showing that the margins are realizable or that individual switches preserve them.
